## Key claims (as stated in source)
- The **WAICO is established as an independent intergovernmental international organization** with international legal personality (Art. 1); all contracting states are Member States.
- **Purposes (Art. 2):** human-centric approach; promote AI for good; open/fair/just/non-discriminatory environment; bridge the AI divide; mitigate risks; safe, secure, ethical, trustworthy AI.
- **Functions (Art. 3):** supply-demand matching platform; capacity-building cooperation; alignment of strategies/governance rules/technical standards; joint open-source ecosystem development; enhance global AI governance and **converge with the UN framework process**; communication with other international organizations. Functions **limited exclusively to the civilian domain of AI**.
- **Fundamental principles (Art. 4):** UN Charter purposes/principles; respect state sovereignty and diversity of civilizations; equality; multilateralism; extensive consultation and joint contribution.
- **Structure (Art. 5):** a **Council** and a **Secretariat**; **Headquarters in Shanghai, PRC**; may establish subsidiary bodies/working groups.
- **Council (Art. 6):** decision-making body; every Member State is a member; annual plenary; Chairperson elected for one year with equitable geographical distribution; each state may designate one official coordinator.
- **Decision-making (Art. 7):** plenary with at least two-thirds of Member States present; **consensus to the furthest extent possible**; failing consensus, **two-thirds majority of members present and voting**; one state one vote.
- **Secretariat (Art. 8):** one **Secretary General** (3-year term, one reterm; national of and nominated by a Member State, appointed by Council); two **Deputy Secretaries General** (same terms).
- **Financing (Art. 9):** annual contributions per an agreed scale of assessment with reference to **Universal Postal Union contribution classes**, plus voluntary contributions and lawful project revenue; no contributions that prejudice its purposes.
- **Membership (Art. 10):** open to all states; signatories during the open-for-signature period are Founding Members; others accede via application and Council approval.
- **Observers (Art. 11):** non-member states and IGOs may be granted observer status; no voting rights.
- **Signature (Art. 14.1):** open for signature **from May 1, 2026 until July 31, 2026** (text truncated at 14.2).
